input.question: "The power to tax is the power to destroy." -Chief Justice John Marshall
input.ground_truth: Taxation can very easily be used to cause people to take some action, or to discourage another. We want people to buy solar panels or health insurance, so we provide tax credits to those that buy the things we want. We don't want people to buy tobacco, so we put high taxes on it. If those taxes were ever set high enough, it could literally shut down the legal tobacco industry. That's the power to destroy an industry through taxation.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: "The power to tax is the power to destroy." -Chief Justice John Marshall

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a toy box, and you love your toys very much. Now, if someone says, “I can take away your toys if I want,” that makes you feel scared and sad, right? Because if they take too many toys, you won’t have any left to play with.

That’s what Chief Justice John Marshall meant. When the government can take away your money with taxes, if they take too much, it can be like taking away all your toys. If they take too much, you might not have enough money for food, clothes, or fun things. So, having the power to tax is a very big and important power, and it must be used carefully, so people are not hurt.
